title: Anticipatory Reversion Framework for Config Deployments with Batch-sensitive Cost Guards
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an anticipatory reversion framework to evaluate and, if necessary, automatically revert configuration changes that negatively impact cost or latency when batching/caching heuristics change. This combines a pre-apply simulation phase, in-flight metric monitoring, and a fast reconciliation path that can restore prior safe state without user intervention. The feature must integrate with Optimize recommendations so config changes that intentionally trade cost for quality are surfaced and require explicit approval.
acceptance_criteria: Pre-apply simulation runs for any config change that touches batching, KV cache, kernel selection, or autoscaling policies and produces a cost/latency delta estimate
Automatic rollback trigger fires when observed 10-minute rolling P95 latency increases > 30% OR cost per token increases > 40% compared to the baseline window
Rollback path restores prior config and PVC snapshots (KV-cache affinity, batching windows) within 90s of trigger detection
All revert actions are recorded in audit logs and surfaced in Console with root-cause hints and a suggested remediation plan
Manual override and hold options available in Console to pause automatic reverts for a specific change/runbook
proposed_design: Step 1: Pre-apply simulator - run a dry-run on a traffic-replay stream (sampled) to estimate batching distribution and KV cache hit-rate; uses lightweight tokenized replay and cost model from Optimize
Step 2: Change canary stage - deploy config to 1-5% capacity with shadow traffic and collect metrics for 10 minutes
Step 3: Threshold detection - compute rolling deltas (latency P50/P95, cost/token, batch size distribution, KV hit-rate). If thresholds breached, mark 'revert_candidate'

Step 4: Safe revert - launch a transactional revert that restores previous config and pinned model variant, reconciles KV cache affinities (best-effort invalidation and warm-up), and drains affected workers with graceful fallback

Step 5: Post-mortem and suggestions - push data into Console and Optimize to create a suggested config patch (e.g., reduce batch_size, enable prefix caching, or increase concurrency) and flag security/audit trail

updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff with SRE, Runtime, and Optimize teams. Agreed thresholds and baseline window (30m pre-deploy). Action: Miguel to prototype simulator interface.
2026-02-18: Prototype simulator completed. Ran replay against a 24h sampled trace; results show KV hit-rate variance is main driver for cost changes on small-context workloads.
2026-02-24: Design review: PM asks to expose 'cost tolerance' per-customer. Added to scope as optional field. Security wants audit entries to include KMS key ID when config touches crypto settings.
2026-02-27: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/rundown/pull/1386 (simulator integration). Requesting review from @sre-team and @optimize
2026-03-01: Canary policy implemented but still defaulting to 0.5% capacity. Need e2e test for revert timing; blocking on ENV for synthetic traffic generation. Estimated 2 more days.
2026-03-01: Miguel assigned follow-up to verify KV cache reconciliation does not leak old keys; added unit tests to ensure no leftover affinity mappings in tenancy metadata.
comments: Asha Patel (2026-02-13): Important to avoid noisy reverts. Propose hysteresis: require 2 consecutive breach windows before auto-revert for non-critical customers.
Samira Khan, SRE (2026-02-19): Simulator looks good. Suggest adding a 'warmup' signal post-revert to avoid immediate reverts on transient spikes.
Dmitri Ivanov, Product (2026-02-24): Add a Console banner explaining why an auto-revert happened and how to proceed. Also request ability to annotate reverts with customer comments.
qa_notes: Create synthetic workload scenarios: small-context chat (avg 128 tokens), long-form generation (avg 1024 tokens), high-concurrency embeddings. Verify revert latency < 90s, no data plane panics, and audit entries contain pre/post config diffs. Run chaos tests where revert path is blocked to validate alerting and manual rollback flows.
